Plugin Debugging

Simulator and Debugging Tool

The simulator simulates most mobile APIs and is equipped with debugging tools. You are advised to debug basic functions and styles in the simulator, and then verify and debug the APIs on mobile devices. The final running effect depends on mobile devices.

Simulator

A simulator provides the following functions:

  • Device simulation (such as size and display ratio)
  • Operation simulation
  • Refreshing
  • Macle JsAPI simulation
  • Gesture simulation

Debugging Tool

With the simulator, the customized Chrome DevTools and extensions such as MAML based on the Chrome DevTools are provided. The following information is displayed by default:

  • MAML: DOM and CSS debugging based on Mini Program elements (not implemented yet)
  • Console: run log and error viewing
  • Sources: source code viewing and breakpoint debugging
  • Network: network resource and request viewing

Debugging in the VS Code

In addition to debugging Mini Program code in the debugger, you can also debug source code in the VS Code.

Prerequisites

You have installed the following software:

  • VS Code
  • Macle MiniProgram Tools VSCode plugin
  • Google Chrome

Configuring the launch.json File

Click the Debugger icon in the Activity Bar to go to the Debug page, click create a launch.json file, and select the Chrome environment.

Replace the content of the generated launch.json file with the corresponding configuration. The following is an example:

{
  // Use IntelliSense to learn about possible attributes.
  // Hover to view descriptions of existing attributes.
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "type": "pwa-chrome",
      "request": "attach",
      "name": "Attach Chrome against localhost",
      "url": "http://localhost:[port]/[projectname][appid]/root/simulator/",
      "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}",
      "port": 31000,
      "sourceMapPathOverrides": {
        "*": "${webRoot}/*"
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "pwa-chrome",
      "request": "launch",
      "name": "Launch Chrome against localhost",
      "url": "http://localhost:[port]/[projectname][appid]/root/simulator/",
      "webRoot": "${workspaceFolder}",
      "sourceMapPathOverrides": {
        "*": "${webRoot}/*"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Note:

  • he attributes of the URL are as follows:

    • Replace port with the actual port number for starting the simulator. The default port number is 30000. If port 30000 is occupied, another port number is used based on the actual port number for starting the simulator.

    • Replace projectname with the actual project name.

    • Replace appid with the actual app ID in the project.

      Example: http://localhost:30000/calculator300s00i1ggac5n020107z1abcdef/root/simulator/

      You can also copy the URL in Google Chrome to replace it.

  • The port attribute in attach mode can be configured on the Settings page. The default value is 31000.

Configuring a Breakpoint

Click the gutter area on the left of the Mini Program source code where the breakpoint is required.

Starting the Debugger

Launch mode is configured in launch.json:

  • Launch mode: Google Chrome is opened and the debugger is automatically attached to the program.

Enabling Launch Mode

  1. Click the simulator function in the plugin to start the simulator.

  2. After the simulator is started, select Launch Chrome against localhost from the RUN AND DEBUG drop-down list, and then press F5 or click the green play button to debug the Mini Program code. (You are advised to change the Google Chrome mode to the mobile mode.)

Simulator + JSSDK debugging

Macle supports emulation debugging and adaptation of JSSDK through simulators. Currently, the webview component cannot be used to navigate to the web debugging page for debugging.

Debugging process:

  1. Introduce Macle JSSDK in H5.
  2. Convert the h5 Mini Program to an Mini Program that can run on the macle engine through a converter.
  3. The simulator opens the converted Mini Program.

The following table lists JSSDK APIs supported by the simulator.

Interface Name Description
ma.miniProgram.close Closes the Mini Program without callback.
ma.chooseImage Photo or Upload
ma.getLocation Obtains the current geographical location information.
ma.previewImage Preview Image
ma.openDocument Open File
ma.getStorage The parameters are consistent with those of the Mini Program interface.
ma.setStorage The parameters are consistent with those of the Mini Program interface.
ma.removeStorage The parameter is consistent with that of the Mini Program interface.
ma.clearStorage The parameters are consistent with those of the Mini Program interface.
ma.getNetworkType Obtain the network status.
ma.scanCode Pull up and scan the QR code. One-dimensional codes are also supported.
ma.callNativeAPI H5 Invoking Native Capabilities
ma.native Invoking native capabilities in H5

This feature supports custom APIs.
